cohort: 100 test queries drawn with random.Random('beir-screen-20261005-scifact').sample(sorted ids, 100); same queries for every added arm.
method: Batched, as hosted Jev rerankers are used: the 50 candidates go in three requests of 17, 17 and 16 passages in retrieval order. Each request has state {query, passages} and one four-level rubric question per passage (the public Jev benchmark's rubric). Rank by expected level; ties by document ID. 17 per request keeps the largest request under the release's 16,384-token default. The Jev arm sends the identical request bodies.
failure_policy: No retries. A failed query stays in the cohort with an empty ranking. Collection stops after three failed queries in a row.
primary: clef minus minilm, nDCG@10 on the attempted queries, paired bootstrap over queries, 95% interval

relevant.instructions: How well does the passage supply the information needed to answer or verify the query?
criteria: The passage is off-topic for the query.
The passage is on a related topic but does not supply what the query asks for.
The passage partly supplies the information needed to answer or verify the query.
The passage fully supplies the information needed to answer or verify the query.

limits: 100 randomly drawn test queries per dataset; intervals are wider than on the full set.
One wording per arm, written before any arm ran; no prompt search.
Candidates are the 50 hybrid results; a reranker cannot recover a document retrieval missed.
Public benchmark text may be in any model's training data.
The release is tested on CUDA. This run is Apple MPS with reference kernels, so its time is not the model's speed and is not reported as one.
